why_refused: Mechanics are clear, meaning is not. Its caller is the tail of RhythmDrum_LoadVoiceParams (labelled VoiceAssign_ProcessRequest), which picks a RhythmDrum_Entries entry for the easy-composer channel and passes byte +2 in HL. Body: k = VoiceAssign_PresetSelToCase[HL] & 7, then word k of three tables goes in DE to RegPreset_Load_Loop (four 0x380A slot pointers), MIDIChan_DispatchDone (copies 7 bytes from the Rhythm ROM header at +0x248 + 7*index to 0x37D1 + 8*channel) and VoiceResolve_CheckAndStore (a flag at 0x387A + channel). Finally VoiceAssign_StoreFinal_Helper maps header byte +0x3D0 through AccTone_LookupByProgram_Table into 0x37CA + channel. What the case k selects and what the per-channel RAM blocks hold are not established, so 'load the channel's pattern parameters' would be a guess.

why_refused: The trigger is clear, the action is not. VoiceCtrl_ParamSetupBytecode calls it on the RHYTHM track (display mode 3) for a recorded tag-0x48 offset-7 event (the rhythm variation) whose byte +5 has bit 4 set. The body saves cursor slot 3 and steps forward to the next 0x81 marker. It then steps back until VoiceState_DataBlock2_Helper3 finds an event of the same kind (0xBn, tag 72, offset 7, byte +5 bit 4), and goes on stepping back over the following ones, calling ToneParam_Evt09_BytecodeHandler_Helper2 on each. Restore and W = 255 when none is found. What bit 4 of byte +5 marks and what ToneParam_Evt09_BytecodeHandler_Helper2 does to those events (it is in the parallel batch, unnamed) are not established.

why_refused: Its use is clear: TempoRingBuf_OnProgramChangeEvent records the program-change record unless it returns W = 1, and it acts only on the RHYTHM track (display mode 3). The decision is not. It feeds the program (0x3722) and bank (0x0E47) to Rhythm_DispatchNote_Tramp and keeps the result in 0x0E40. It compares that with 0x0E3F (set by ToneParam_HandlerTable_BC_Helper4's search back over the track) and, depending on the comparison and the unit counters 0x0D5A / 0x0E6B, records the event itself, runs ToneParam_HandlerTable_BC_Helper7/8, or rejects with GLOBAL_ERROR_CODE 25 (SoundCtrl_SendCommand 0xEE). What 0x0E3F/0x0E40 hold is not established (a time signature would fit but is not shown), and neither is what error 25 is.

why_refused: Mechanics are clear, the meaning of the result is not. It is a register-preserving call of RegBitManip_Handler_4_Helper, which copies the three bytes at 0x90EA into +3..+5 of a 6-byte stack record, runs SndParam_ComputeVoiceIndex on it and leaves +0..+2 at 0x90EE. Both callers load 0x90EA with a part's word (MidiStream_HandleNoteCC_Body: word 0 of the part record (0x90F2)[part]) and 0x90EC with the part. They then pass (0x90EE) as DE with dispatch code 0x81 and (0x90F0) as E to MIDI_DispatchCC_Guarded / MIDI_ClearGuardAndDispatchCC. That looks like an outgoing bank/program translation, the reverse of MidiStream_ResolveVoiceIndex. But what the part word is, what SndParam_ComputeVoiceIndex produces and what dispatch code 0x81 sends (MidiCC_ChannelDispatch_TableA) are not established.

why_refused: Mechanics are clear, meaning is not, as for its sibling SoundEvt_LongPacketHandler_DispatchTbl_Target1_Helper (refused in batch l). VoiceSlot_StatusRet calls it on the chord track (display mode 0) for a 0x9n event. When the cursor byte is exactly 0x90 it does this: sets 0x28B3 bit 6 and saves cursor slot 1; drains SeqBuf (SeqBuf_ReadByte until 0xFFFF); sends note-offs (VoiceCtrl_SendNoteOffSequence); for each following 0x90 event at the same clock (0x0DC2) appends five bytes to SeqBuf {status, 0, note, 64, (0x0EEE) - 1}; then runs VoiceAlloc_ScoopDisplayProcess and restores slot 1. 'Sound the chord at the cursor' fits, but what VoiceAlloc_ScoopDisplayProcess does with the SeqBuf records is not established.

header: Builds the event bitmap of the displayed grid row: puts the cursor back at the row start ((0x0DE8)/(0x0DEC)), clears 0x372E-0x3739 and walks the events to the row end ((0x0DEA)/(0x0DED)); each event sets bit clock/12 in the byte of its beat (0x3732 + beat, advanced at each 0x81 marker), an END marker 0x82 records its column in 0x0F5B with 0x0F5A = 2, and 0x84 stops the walk. Basis: callers + body -- VoiceSlot_TableSetup calls it once it has found the row's start and end; 0x3732 is the 32-bit step bitmap whose bit (0x370F) - 1 marks the cursor step.
